title: Book Three · Chapter 74: The Words After Class
story:
A few weeks pass. Winter is nearly over, but the morning wind is still cold.

Leo's twelfth reply reaches Ronan before school. It tells him about the station shops and a man who sells secondhand books there.

Ronan reads it once and puts it beside his pen. He will answer after his school work.

In class, the teacher gives them a short scene to read aloud. One person is a shopkeeper. The other keeps adding things to an order.

Ronan reads the shopkeeper's part. Kai is the customer.

“Three apples,” Kai says.

“Three apples.”

“And two pears.”

Ronan picks up an imaginary pear, then another. He puts them on an imaginary counter with great care.

Kai looks at the page.

“And one more thing.”

Ronan turns slowly toward him.

“A larger bag?”

That line is not on the page. Kai laughs and loses his next words. The teacher waits with a smile.

“Finish the scene,” she says.

Ronan holds up the imaginary bag. Kai finds his place and reads again.

Across the desk, Anna is laughing quietly. Ronan sees her face and almost misses his own next line.

At lunch, Kai asks him to bring that voice to the real shops.

“They may charge for it,” Ronan says.

Anna puts her lunch box down.

“A larger price for the larger bag.”

The three laugh. Then Lin comes over with a book. She and Anna want to look at one page before the afternoon lesson.

Ronan goes outside with Kai. They play until the bell, and he does not get another quiet moment with Anna.

After the last lesson, he waits near the stairs. Anna comes down with her bag over one shoulder.

“Are you waiting for someone?” she asks.

“You.”

Anna stops beside him.

Ronan moves his book from one hand to the other. The words in class were easy. These are slower.

“Do you have time on Saturday afternoon?”

“After two.”

“A walk in the park?”

“With Kai and Lin?”

“Just us, if you want.”

Anna looks at him for a moment. Then she smiles.

“Half past two. Near the tree?”

“Yes.”

They walk to the gate together. Anna tells him about her Saturday morning run with Lin. Ronan has one delivery for Mum before noon.

The afternoon is free for both of them.

At the crossing, Anna turns toward home. Ronan stands still until a bicycle passes. Then he takes his own road.

At home, he writes half past two beside Saturday in his notebook. He does not add a wall, a window, or a list of school questions.

He puts the notebook down and opens Leo's letter again. For once, the station shops seem far away from the thing he wants to say next.
studyGuide:
## 词句提示

scene＝一段戏、场景；shopkeeper＝店主；imaginary＝想象中的；read aloud＝出声朗读。

## 理解问题

1. Ronan怎样让课堂对话有了轻松的变化？
2. 他约Anna星期六做什么？这次和以往四个人的安排有什么不同？

## 读句子

**Anna stops beside him.**

拆开看：Anna / stops / beside him.

Anna／停下脚步／停在他身边。
